Research question: "What analyses or measurements would best test whether AP-1 acts as a cellular memory mechanism?"

Propose 5 distinct, concrete ideas (analyses, measurements, or experiments) that a research lab could pursue to address this question. For each idea give a short title and a description of one or two sentences.

ideas.title: Random-string scrambling control for memory readout
ideas.description: Like the material, which is a random character string with no recoverable signal, build a null model by shuffling AP-1 motif positions and ChIP/ATAC labels across the genome. Compare real persistence of AP-1 binding after stimulus withdrawal against this shuffled null to show that retained accessibility is not chance.

ideas.title: Stimulus-withdrawal time-course of AP-1 occupancy and accessibility
ideas.description: Expose cells (e.g., fibroblasts or macrophages) to a transient stimulus, remove it, and track CUT&RUN for FOS/JUN plus ATAC-seq at days 0 to 14. Sites that stay open and AP-1 bound long after FOS/JUN transcript levels return to baseline indicate memory.

ideas.title: Acute AP-1 degradation after priming vs. before
ideas.description: Use degron-tagged JUN/FOS (dTAG) or dominant-negative A-FOS to remove AP-1 either during priming or only during rechallenge. If memory persists when AP-1 is removed after priming, it's held by other factors. If it is lost, AP-1 maintains the memory.

ideas.title: Secondary stimulation response with motif mutation
ideas.description: Use CRISPR editing or dCas9 interference to mutate AP-1 motifs at primed enhancers, then measure the enhanced transcriptional response to a second stimulus by RNA-seq or reporter assays. This tests whether specific sites are necessary for faster, stronger re-induction.

ideas.title: Single-cell multiome and lineage tracing of memory inheritance
ideas.description: Perform paired scRNA/ATAC on clonally related sister cells after priming and several divisions. Test whether AP-1-linked accessibility is inherited more similarly within clones than across them, and whether it predicts each cell's rechallenge response.
